# Vendored Packages

This directory contains source-vendored copies of the Cordis framework and its foundation libraries. They are copied into this monorepo instead of being depended on via npm, so that the harness fully owns its framework layer (auditable, patchable, pinned).

All vendored packages use the **`@deepseek-ai` scope** (`cordis` → `@deepseek-ai/cordis`, `@cordisjs/plugin-<x>` → `@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-<x>`). The manifest table records upstream versions and source commits; each package manifest carries its Harness release version and publication metadata. References to vendored packages use `workspace:~`, so local builds resolve the workspace packages and published ranges permit patch updates within the same minor version. Upstream MIT `LICENSE` files are preserved in each package directory.

This file covers the manifest, the local-modification log, and the procedure for **updating** an existing vendored package. To **add a new** one, see the cookbook guide: [docs/cookbook/adding-a-vendored-package.md](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-vendored-package.md).

## Manifest

The seven Cordis packages come from one upstream commit, `01b396240ce47cf2779c40af9bc445bb748fe112` of https://github.com/cordiverse/cordis ("chore: bump versions", 2026-10-21), the commit of the latest npm releases. Cosmokit and Schemastery keep their earlier pins.

Third-party dependencies of the vendored packages stay on npm: `@standard-schema/spec`, `yaml`, `chokidar`, `picomatch`, `@babel/code-frame`, `supports-color`, `node-addon-require-builtin`.

Intentionally **not** vendored (verified unused by this set): `reggol`, `@cordisjs/utils`, `@cordisjs/element`, `@cordisjs/unyaml` (dev-time YAML import hook only).

DSH profiles run `@deepseek-ai/dsh-hmr`, not the vendored HMR package. Both provide `ctx.hmr.watch()`, which Include uses to refresh its file; DSH HMR owns realpath canonicalization, watcher readiness and exact-path watching for its profile.

## Local modifications

Keep this log exhaustive — every divergence from upstream must be listed. The identifiers are stable across syncs. Upstream supplies the behavior of the retired identifiers V8, V9, V12, V13, V14, V18, V19 and V21, whose patches were removed when syncing to `01b3962`.

- V1. **`hmr/src/index.ts`**: removed the `./locales/en-US.yml` / `./locales/zh-CN.yml` imports, the `.i18n({...})` call on the `Config` schema, and the `src/locales/` directory. Rationale: those imports require a runtime YAML loader hook (`@cordisjs/unyaml`) that we do not vendor; the i18n texts only localize config descriptions.
- V2. **All `package.json` files**: regenerated for Harness releases with scoped names, release versions, publication metadata, precise bundled-runtime and `lib/types/**/*.d.ts` / `.d.ts.map` file entries, source exports where applicable, and declaration metadata pointing at `lib/types`. References within the vendored set use `workspace:~`. HMR declares `esbuild` as a direct dev dependency for its imported `BuildFailure` type, Loader requires `node-addon-require-builtin@^0.1.9` to match published app runtimes, and Include takes upstream's `yaml` dependency. Include declares no HMR dependency (see V25).
- V3. **All `tsconfig.json` files**: regenerated to extend the repo-root `tsconfig.base.json`, emit TypeScript intermediates to `lib/types`, and declare project references matching each package's imports.
- V4. **Relative specifiers**: upstream now writes explicit `.ts` specifiers (cordiverse/cordis#125); `logger-console/src/{index,browser}.ts` keep `./shared.ts` where upstream writes `./shared.js`, so TypeScript rewrites emitted JS to `.js` while declarations keep NodeNext-safe `.ts` specifiers.
- V5. **`loader/tsdown.config.ts`, `schemastery/tsdown.config.ts` and `logger-console/tsdown.config.ts`**: ours, not upstream files — per-package build-shape overrides (single-bundle Loader output; dual ESM+CJS output; separate node/browser entries) for the repo-root tsdown build. They read the JS emitted under `lib/types` and then write the publish runtime entries under `lib/`. Like the regenerated tsconfigs, they are not part of the upstream sync surface.
- V6. **`cordis/src/fiber.ts` lifecycle hardening**: closes reentrant disposal gaps upstream leaves open. An effect's owner-list wrapper is registered before its setup body runs, so an unload begun from inside setup awaits setup and every collected cleanup; synchronous setup failure removes the wrapper and rolls back collected cleanup. Async cleanup stays owner-visible until quiescence, and Cordis's internal effect composition joins an already-running cleanup while repeated public disposer calls retain their upstream single-shot result. Effect creation is rejected while the owner is `UNLOADING` (while `PENDING` and `LOADING` remain legal), preventing cleanup-time registrations from escaping the unload snapshot; this includes the period in which an unloading provider waits for its dependents (upstream's provider-after-dependent teardown), so a late asynchronous continuation of the provider cannot start new work. Effects registered through a service method belong to the calling context, not to the provider. Child fibers register and receive their parent-owned disposer before `internal/plugin` publication, resolve dependency declarations added by that notification before activation, drain effects attached while pending or failed, and contain teardown-notification failures per observer (through the per-listener `events.dispatch()`), so one callback cannot starve peers or interrupt ownership cleanup. Upstream supplies the stale-epoch guard that skips plugin execution after reentrant disposal. Covered by `packages/extensions/tool-cordis/tests/cordis-lifecycle.spec.ts`.
- V7. **Cordis, Loader and Timer JSDoc enrichment**: added `@param`/`@returns` tags and contract documentation (disposal semantics, waterfall veto, bail conditions, error cases) across the public plugin-author surface — `Context` (class, statics, and the `Context` interface properties incl. `[Context.root]`), module re-exports, shared utility helpers, `EventsService`, `Fiber`, `RegistryService`, `ReflectService`, `Service`, `LoggerService`, `ValidationError` and their `declare module './context.ts'` overloads. `Fiber.config` is declared as a documented field instead of upstream's constructor parameter property, so the reference generator lists it. Loader documentation covers `loader/src/{index,internal,config/entry,config/group,config/isolate,config/tree,config/utils}.ts`, including entry ownership, tree mutation and `commit()` reporting, source locations, and the `!!js` discriminator. Timer retains its local class and helper summaries; its README is local documentation because the upstream package has none, and the Cordis, Loader, Include and HMR READMEs are local documentation too. Comment-only; no code changes. Motivation: the website API-reference generator renders these docs and hard-errors on undocumented members.
- V10. **Vendored Node-compatible TypeScript**: marked erased imports explicitly (`import type` or inline `type` modifiers) across `cordis`, `loader`, `include`, `hmr`, and `schemastery` so Node's native TypeScript transform does not request types as runtime exports. Schemastery's source uses an ESM default export and its package declares `type: module`. Conditional exports select `.mjs` for import and `.cjs` for require; without them, concurrent imports under module-hook hosts reach the CJS entry and can race its require of ESM Cosmokit (`ERR_REQUIRE_ESM_RACE_CONDITION`).
- V11. **`include/src/{index,patch}.ts` patch and dialect exports**: Include exports upstream's pure `applyPatches(data, patches, warn)` with `PatchOptions` and `PatchResult`, and its YAML dialect as `parseEntryYaml(content)` / `stringifyEntryYaml(data)`, which Include's own file writes use. `dsh --dump-config`, profile composition, compatibility preflight and config tooling therefore compose and print exactly what an Include mounts without booting a tree; config tooling must never reimplement (and drift from) the patch algorithm or the dialect. The `!!js` tag rejects an empty expression, which would otherwise evaluate to `undefined` silently, so the file read fails loud with its location. Public patch and Include config fields carry JSDoc for config tooling. Covered by `packages/boot/app-boot/tests/{config-dump,user-patches}.spec.ts`.
- V15. **Configuration access across `cordis/src/{events,fiber}.ts`, `loader/src/index.ts` and `include/src/index.ts`**: upstream retains raw `Fiber.config`, resolves it through `internal/config(fiber, next)` on every activation and reports accepted raw config through `internal/commit`. Locally, `Fiber.effectiveConfig` records the object the latest activation passed to the plugin (undefined before the first activation, readable after unload), and the resolution step is the public `Fiber.resolveConfig(config)` instead of upstream's private `_resolve`, so settings, the config editor and volatile commits can read the running object and validate candidates without publishing them. Both use the canonical fiber when reached through a registry wrapper. Include declares the `EntryGroup.key` tree-carrier marker (as Group does): its config is entry and patch lists, so Loader interpolation keeps it literal and a `!!js` expression inside a nested row's config resolves lazily in that row's own fiber (Include's own `path` therefore stays literal too). Loader's self-dispose handler also skips persistence while the entry's tree owner is `UNLOADING`, not only after its uid is cleared. Covered by `scripts/cordis-config-access.spec.ts`, `packages/boot/app-boot/tests/{app-boot,user-patches}.spec.ts`, `packages/boot/cmdline/tests/cmdline.spec.ts`, `apps/cli/tests/web-agent-presets.e2e.ts`, and the built custom-profile cases in `apps/cli/tests/built-bin.e2e.ts`.
- V16. **`cordis/package.json` publishes `src`**: added `src` to the `files` list, joining the other eight vendored packages. Cordis declares `"./src/*": "./src/*"` in its exports, so a tarball without `src` publishes an export map pointing at absent files; the release change judgement also reads `files` to decide whether a diff reaches the payload, and a package whose only published paths are build output has no tracked path to match.
- V17. **`@deepseek-ai` rescope**: every vendored manifest `name`, every internal dependency entry among the vendored set, and every module specifier that reaches them use the scoped names in the manifest table's `npm name` column. Directory names, version numbers, and dependency ranges are unchanged, and no upstream runtime identifier is renamed — `Symbol.for('schemastery')` and Schemastery's `vendor:` metadata field keep their upstream values. Re-apply with `pnpm run rescope-vendor --apply` after a sync; the table's two name columns are the mapping, restated for consumers in [docs/rescope.md](../docs/rescope.md).
- V20. **`loader/src/config/entry.ts` fiber identity**: stores the original fiber from the registry result's context where upstream Loader stores its PromiseLike wrapper. A volatile commit assigns `fiber.config`, which on a wrapper would only shadow the canonical field, and DSH compares entry fibers with registry fibers by identity. Covered by `packages/boot/hmr/tests/modules.spec.ts` and the built profile reload regression in `apps/cli/tests/built-bin.e2e.ts`. The vendored HMR keeps upstream's assignment of the wrapper.
- V22. **Volatile config across `cosmokit`, `schemastery`, `cordis`, and `loader`**: Cosmokit supplies immutable references and framework-owned commits; `deepEqual` treats two references as equal, propagates strict comparison into arrays, compares every array slot with holes treated as undefined, handles cycles conservatively, compares URLs by normalized href, and compares other opaque objects by identity in strict mode. Schemastery adds `.volatile()`, optional/default inference, placement validation without eager lazy-schema expansion (a lazy inner is validated once when built), metadata-free serialized node compatibility, serialized metadata, reference-aware simplification, unsupported volatile values reported as `ValidationError` with their path, and `.default()` accepting the raw input type `Partial<S>` because a volatile field makes the output type carry references. Loader's `internal/commit` listener calls `simplify` with its schema receiver (`unparse.call`), an independent fix for the unbound-`this` call. Cordis re-exports the consumer types `Volatile` and `VolatileSnapshot` without changing Fiber lifecycle. Loader compares raw options strictly in `Entry.update`; for a config-only change on an active fiber it calls the pure `equalExceptVolatile` function in `config/diff.ts`, which narrows the Standard Schema to Schemastery's `Schema` type (a type-only `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` dependency of `loader`) and recursively skips fixed volatile paths using schema metadata without executing config hooks or validation. Missing or null object nodes compare using their declared defaults, including nodes without volatile descendants; schema backedges retain raw comparison. Entry passes its actual schema and preserves ordinary context and custom-update lifecycles. For a volatile-only change, `Entry._commitVolatile` assigns the raw config, re-parses it through `Fiber.resolveConfig()`, compares ordinary effective values, commits references and emits the instance-local `loader/volatile-update` declared in `loader/src/index.ts`; a changed ordinary effective value falls back to the ordinary remount, and an invalid candidate is logged while the raw config stays retained for the next activation. Cosmokit provides reference enumeration and commits. The package READMEs document these additions; schema tests live in `scripts/volatile-config.spec.ts`, Loader runtime and real-file tests in `scripts/loader-volatile-update.spec.ts`, and code replacement tests in the HMR module suite.
- V23. **`loader/src/config/entry.ts` module identity**: retains each entry's raw import result as `moduleNamespace`, before plugin export normalization. DSH HMR matches that object to Node's cached module namespace and updates it after a successful reload. `EntryTree.import()` keeps its existing arguments and return value; `loader/README.md` documents the additive field.
- V24. **`timer/locale/{en,zh}.json` display metadata**: local English and Chinese titles and descriptions for the Settings plugin inventory. `timer/package.json` exports and publishes these locale resources.
- V25. **`include/src/index.ts` structural HMR access**: upstream imports `@cordisjs/plugin-hmr`'s types for `ctx.hmr.watch()`. Both HMR providers declare their own `Context.hmr`, so a program that sees Include and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-hmr` would carry two conflicting declarations; Include instead reads the service with `ctx.get('hmr')` as the exported `HmrWatch` shape, the `watch()` contract both providers implement.
- V26. **`loader/src/config/entry.ts` re-initialization waits for the previous fiber**: upstream's provider-after-dependent teardown keeps a disabled entry's services registered until its dependents have unloaded, while `Entry.update` disposes without waiting. Re-enabling the entry before that finishes would start a new fiber whose `provide` collides with the old registration (`service "…" has been registered`), so `_init` awaits the previous fiber's settlement after the import and before patching the context. Covered by `packages/settings/settings/tests/configuration.spec.ts`.
- V27. **`cordis/src/events.ts` keeps `EventsService.dispatch()` undeprecated**: upstream marks `dispatch()` `@deprecated` without offering a replacement API. DSH resolves the filtered listener set through it in 14 places to deliver notifications that contain each listener's failure separately, which `emit()` (one synchronous throw stops later listeners) and `parallel()` (one aggregate rejection) do not provide. Liwa maintains its fork independently of upstream, so the deprecation carries no migration path for us; the tag is removed and the method keeps its documented contract.

### Resolver adaptations

Relative to the resolver source of Loader `1.0.0-rc.9`:

- **Web build imports:** `loader/src/resolve.ts`, and the `node:url` import that `loader/src/config/tree.ts` gained upstream, use default imports for Node builtin modules to support the Web shell's browser externalization. The shell supplies its own module loader.
- **Package-scope cache keys:** `loader/src/resolve.ts` normalizes directory paths with `path.resolve()` before finding the package scope. A root config and a nested config in the same package therefore share the same cached resolver promise and helper-file write. Covered by `scripts/cordis-loader-resolve.spec.ts`.

## Sync procedure

To update a vendored package from upstream:

1. In the upstream checkout, note `git rev-parse HEAD`, or the commit of the npm release being synced.
2. Copy the package's `src/` (and `bin.js`, `README.md`, `LICENSE` if changed) over the vendored directory. A three-way merge with the previous upstream source as the base keeps the local modifications visible as conflicts.
3. Re-apply the local modifications listed above (or drop them if upstream made them unnecessary — update the log either way).
4. Update the version and commit hash in the manifest table.
5. Run `pnpm install && pnpm run test && pnpm run build` at the repo root.
